title: "8. How similar are the benchmark references to each other?"

Relationships inside the benchmark set, for the HMA domain and the effector
separately and by both sequence and structure, so accuracy differences between
targets can be read against how related those targets are.

One row per distinct protein rather than per PDB entry. The 18 entries are 18
complexes, not 18 distinct chains. AVR-PikD appears six times and AVR-PikE three
times, and the same holds for the HMAs. Plotting per entry would fill the matrix
with 100% cells that only restate which complexes share a chain. The 18 entries
collapse to 9 distinct HMA domains and 7 distinct effectors. Each axis is
labelled by its own chain alone, since the partner chain is irrelevant to that
axis.

The two chains are treated separately because the set is close to a grid, an
allelic effector series against a handful of HMA backgrounds. Two entries can
share an effector exactly while their HMAs differ by a third of their residues,
and a single combined distance would hide that.

Chains are grouped by the protein name in the manifest description. Within
every group the pairwise substitution count is zero, so each group is genuinely
one sequence. Identity within a group sometimes falls below 100% only because
constructs were modelled to different boundaries, which shows up as gap
positions rather than substitutions. The one exception is a substitution between
6R8M and 7A8W in a region 6R8K does not model, which is a coverage artefact.

Sequence identity comes from `reference_similarity.csv`, built by
`bin/compute_reference_similarity.py`. Chains are read from the deposited
coordinates and globally aligned with EMBOSS `needle` at its published defaults,
EBLOSUM62 with gap open 10.0 and gap extend 0.5. Identity counts literal residue
matches, so these are true identities rather than similarities. The substitution
matrix places the alignment but plays no part in scoring.

Percent identity has no single agreed definition, and the denominator can move a
number by tens of percentage points, so the CSV carries both conventions.
`*_identity` divides by the shorter ungapped chain, which is what the figures
use, since several references are the same protein resolved to different
boundaries and should not be penalised for residues the other entry did not
model. `*_identity_over_alignment` divides by the full alignment length, which
is the number `needle` itself reports.

Structural similarity is TM-align via `tmtools` on Cα coordinates of the
deposited chains. TM-score runs from 0 to 1, is length-normalised, and by
convention above 0.5 means the same fold while below about 0.17 is the
random-pair baseline. It comes from a structural superposition and needs no
sequence alignment, which matters because the MAX effectors are a structurally
conserved but sequence-unrelated family
([de Guillen et al. 2015](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.ppat.1005228)), so a
sequence-guided superposition would assume what is being tested.

For both measures the value plotted between two groups is the median over all
cross-group entry pairs, which averages out construct-boundary noise rather
than depending on which entry is picked as a representative. Both normalise by
the shorter chain, so neither penalises a construct for residues it does not
model.

Clustering is average linkage (UPGMA) on percent-difference or 1 minus TM-score
distance, implemented in NumPy. Ties break by index, so the ordering is
deterministic.

```{python}
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "../../bin")
from _analysis_common import *

import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

from Bio.PDB import PDBParser
from Bio.Data.PDBData import protein_letters_3to1 as THREE_TO_ONE
from tmtools import tm_align

sim = pd.read_csv(DATA_DIR / "reference_similarity.csv")
manifest = pd.read_csv(MANIFEST, sep="\t")
manifest = manifest[manifest["tier"] == TIER]

PDBS = sorted(set(sim["pdb_a"]) | set(sim["pdb_b"]))
DESC = dict(zip(manifest["pdb"], manifest["description"]))
SYSTEM = dict(zip(manifest["pdb"], manifest["system"]))
IDX = {p: i for i, p in enumerate(PDBS)}

CHAINS = [("receptor_identity", 0, "HMA Domain"),
          ("effector_identity", 1, "Effector")]
CHAIN_ID = {0: "A", 1: "B"}          # receptor, effector
TM_FOLD_THRESHOLD = 0.5

# The manifest descriptions are written for a complex table, so they carry
# wording that is redundant once each axis is one chain. Shortened for the
# axis labels only; the grouping key is still the manifest name.
SHORT_NAME = {
    "ancestral Pik1-HMA (ancHMA-Pikp)": "ancHMA-Pikp",
    "engineered RGA5-HMA mutant": "RGA5-HMA (mut)",
    "engineered Pikp1-HMA (NK-KE)": "Pikp1-HMA (NK-KE)",
    "engineered Pikp1-HMA (SNK-EKE)": "Pikp1-HMA (SNK-EKE)",
}


def short(name):
    return SHORT_NAME.get(name, name)


def chain_name(pdb, side):
    """Receptor (side 0) or effector (side 1) name from the manifest description."""
    d = DESC.get(pdb, pdb)
    return d.split(" / ")[side].strip() if " / " in d else d


def group_members(side):
    """Distinct protein name -> the PDB entries carrying it, commonest first."""
    members = {}
    for p in PDBS:
        members.setdefault(chain_name(p, side), []).append(p)
    return members, sorted(members, key=lambda k: (-len(members[k]), k))
```

```{python}
def entry_matrix(col):
    """Symmetric per-entry percent-identity matrix, self-identity on the diagonal."""
    m = np.full((len(PDBS), len(PDBS)), np.nan)
    np.fill_diagonal(m, 100.0)
    for _, r in sim.iterrows():
        i, j = IDX[r["pdb_a"]], IDX[r["pdb_b"]]
        m[i, j] = m[j, i] = r[col]
    return m


_seq_cache = {}


def grouped_identity(col, side):
    """Distinct-protein identity matrix, median over cross-group entry pairs."""
    if (col, side) in _seq_cache:
        return _seq_cache[(col, side)]
    ent = entry_matrix(col)
    members, names = group_members(side)
    n = len(names)
    m = np.full((n, n), 100.0)
    for a in range(n):
        for b in range(a + 1, n):
            m[a, b] = m[b, a] = float(np.median(
                [ent[IDX[x], IDX[y]]
                 for x in members[names[a]] for y in members[names[b]]]))
    _seq_cache[(col, side)] = (names, [len(members[k]) for k in names], m)
    return _seq_cache[(col, side)]
```

```{python}
REFS = REPO_ROOT / "data" / "complexes_for_benchmarking"
_parser = PDBParser(QUIET=True)
_trace_cache = {}
_tm_cache = {}


def ca_trace(pdb, chain):
    """Cα coordinates and the matching one-letter sequence for one chain."""
    st = _parser.get_structure("x", REFS / f"{pdb}.pdb")
    xyz, seq = [], []
    for res in st[0][chain]:
        if res.id[0] != " " or "CA" not in res:
            continue
        aa = (THREE_TO_ONE.get(res.get_resname().capitalize())
              or THREE_TO_ONE.get(res.get_resname()))
        if aa is None:
            continue
        xyz.append(res["CA"].coord)
        seq.append(aa)
    return np.array(xyz, dtype=float), "".join(seq)


def tm_pair(pdb_a, pdb_b, side):
    """TM-score normalised by the shorter chain, and the superposition RMSD."""
    for p in (pdb_a, pdb_b):
        _trace_cache.setdefault((p, side), ca_trace(p, CHAIN_ID[side]))
    xa, sa = _trace_cache[(pdb_a, side)]
    xb, sb = _trace_cache[(pdb_b, side)]
    r = tm_align(xa, xb, sa, sb)
    # Normalising by the shorter chain is the larger of the two values.
    return max(r.tm_norm_chain1, r.tm_norm_chain2), r.rmsd


def grouped_tm(side):
    """Distinct-protein TM-score matrix, median over cross-group entry pairs."""
    if side in _tm_cache:
        return _tm_cache[side]
    members, names = group_members(side)
    n = len(names)
    m = np.full((n, n), 1.0)
    rms = np.zeros((n, n))
    for a in range(n):
        for b in range(a + 1, n):
            vals = [tm_pair(x, y, side)
                    for x in members[names[a]] for y in members[names[b]]]
            m[a, b] = m[b, a] = float(np.median([v[0] for v in vals]))
            rms[a, b] = rms[b, a] = float(np.median([v[1] for v in vals]))
    _tm_cache[side] = (names, [len(members[k]) for k in names], m, rms)
    return _tm_cache[side]
```

```{python}
def upgma(dist):
    """Average-linkage clustering. Returns (merges, leaf_order).

    merges is a list of (left, right, height, size), where left and right index
    either a leaf (< n) or an earlier merge (n + k), matching the SciPy linkage
    convention so the drawing code below is conventional.
    """
    n = len(dist)
    d = dist.astype(float).copy()
    np.fill_diagonal(d, np.inf)
    active = list(range(n))
    sizes = {i: 1 for i in range(n)}
    members = {i: [i] for i in range(n)}
    merges = []

    for step in range(n - 1):
        best, pair = np.inf, None
        for ai, a in enumerate(active):
            for b in active[ai + 1:]:
                if d[a, b] < best:
                    best, pair = d[a, b], (a, b)
        a, b = pair
        new = n + step
        merges.append((a, b, best, sizes[a] + sizes[b]))

        d = np.pad(d, ((0, 1), (0, 1)), constant_values=np.inf)
        for c in active:
            if c in (a, b):
                continue
            # UPGMA: mean over all cross-cluster leaf pairs, i.e. size-weighted.
            d[new, c] = d[c, new] = ((d[a, c] * sizes[a] + d[b, c] * sizes[b])
                                     / (sizes[a] + sizes[b]))
        active = [c for c in active if c not in (a, b)] + [new]
        sizes[new] = sizes[a] + sizes[b]
        members[new] = members[a] + members[b]

    return merges, members[n + len(merges) - 1]


def draw_dendrogram(ax, merges, order, n, threshold=None):
    """Draw merges as U shapes. Leaves sit at 0.5, 1.5, ... in `order`."""
    pos = {leaf: i + 0.5 for i, leaf in enumerate(order)}
    height = {i: 0.0 for i in range(n)}
    for k, (a, b, h, _) in enumerate(merges):
        xa, xb = pos[a], pos[b]
        ax.plot([xa, xa, xb, xb], [height[a], h, h, height[b]],
                color="black", lw=1.0)
        pos[n + k], height[n + k] = (xa + xb) / 2.0, h
    if threshold is not None:
        ax.axhline(threshold, ls="--", color="crimson", lw=1)
    ax.set_xlim(0, n)
    ax.set_ylim(0, max(m[2] for m in merges) * 1.05)
    ax.set_xticks([])
    ax.tick_params(labelsize=8)
    for side in ("top", "right", "bottom"):
        ax.spines[side].set_visible(False)


def draw_heatmap(ax, names, counts, mat, order, cmap, vmin, vmax, fmt, flip_at):
    """Identity or TM-score matrix, ordered by its dendrogram."""
    n = len(names)
    ordered = mat[np.ix_(order, order)]
    im = ax.imshow(ordered, cmap=cmap, vmin=vmin, vmax=vmax, extent=[0, n, n, 0])
    ax.set_xticks(np.arange(n) + 0.5)
    ax.set_yticks(np.arange(n) + 0.5)
    ax.set_xticklabels([short(names[i]) for i in order], rotation=40, ha="right",
                       fontsize=8)
    ax.set_yticklabels([f"{short(names[i])}  (n={counts[i]})" for i in order],
                       fontsize=8)
    for r in range(n):
        for c in range(n):
            v = ordered[r, c]
            ax.text(c + 0.5, r + 0.5, fmt(v), ha="center", va="center",
                    fontsize=7.5, color="white" if v < flip_at else "black")
    ax.set_xticks(np.arange(n + 1), minor=True)
    ax.set_yticks(np.arange(n + 1), minor=True)
    ax.grid(which="minor", color="white", lw=0.6)
    ax.tick_params(which="minor", length=0)
    return im
```

## Sequence and structure, both chains

Panel A is sequence identity and panel B is TM-score. Within each panel
the HMA domain is on the left and the effector on the right. Every dendrogram
sets the row and column order of the heatmap beneath it, and the count after
each label is how many of the 18 complexes carry that chain. The dashed line on
the panel B dendrograms is the 0.5 same-fold threshold.

```{python}
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(14.5, 13.0))
# Nested so the gap between a dendrogram and its own heatmap can stay tight
# while the gap between panel A and panel B stays wide.
outer = fig.add_gridspec(2, 1, hspace=0.20, left=0.17, right=0.86,
                         top=0.955, bottom=0.055)
panels = {}
pairs = []
images = {}

for row, kind in enumerate(["seq", "str"]):
    inner = outer[row].subgridspec(2, 2, height_ratios=[1, 3.4], hspace=0.02,
                                   wspace=0.5)
    for col_i, (col, side, title) in enumerate(CHAINS):
        if kind == "seq":
            names, counts, mat = grouped_identity(col, side)
            merges, order = upgma(100.0 - mat)
            thresh, ylab = None, "Percent\ndifference"
            cmap, vmin, vmax, fmt, flip = "viridis", 0, 100, lambda v: f"{v:.0f}", 55
        else:
            names, counts, mat, _rms = grouped_tm(side)
            merges, order = upgma(1.0 - mat)
            thresh, ylab = 1 - TM_FOLD_THRESHOLD, "1 - TM-score"
            cmap, vmin, vmax, fmt, flip = "magma", 0, 1, lambda v: f"{v:.2f}", 0.6

        panels[(kind, title)] = (names, counts, mat, order)
        ax_d = fig.add_subplot(inner[0, col_i])
        draw_dendrogram(ax_d, merges, order, len(names), threshold=thresh)
        ax_d.set_ylabel(ylab, fontsize=9)
        ax_d.set_title(f"{title}, {'sequence' if kind == 'seq' else 'structure'}",
                       fontsize=12, pad=8)
        ax_h = fig.add_subplot(inner[1, col_i])
        images[kind] = draw_heatmap(ax_h, names, counts, mat, order, cmap,
                                    vmin, vmax, fmt, flip)
        pairs.append((kind, ax_d, ax_h))

# imshow keeps a square aspect, so each heatmap is drawn narrower than the slot
# it was given. Pull every dendrogram onto its heatmap's real width.
fig.canvas.draw()
row_extent = {}
for kind, ax_d, ax_h in pairs:
    bh = ax_h.get_position(original=False)
    bd = ax_d.get_position(original=False)
    ax_d.set_position([bh.x0, bd.y0, bh.width, bd.height])
    lo, hi = row_extent.get(kind, (1.0, 0.0))
    row_extent[kind] = (min(lo, bh.y0), max(hi, bh.y1))

for kind, label, cbar_label in [("seq", "A", "Percent identity"),
                                ("str", "B", "TM-score")]:
    lo, hi = row_extent[kind]
    cax = fig.add_axes([0.885, lo, 0.014, (hi - lo) * 0.62])
    cb = fig.colorbar(images[kind], cax=cax, label=cbar_label)
    if kind == "str":
        cb.ax.axhline(TM_FOLD_THRESHOLD, color="crimson", lw=1.4)
    top = max(ax_d.get_position().y1 for k, ax_d, _ in pairs if k == kind)
    fig.text(0.015, top + 0.035, label, fontsize=19, fontweight="bold",
             va="top")

save_fig(fig, "reference_similarity_matrices")
plt.show()
```

```{python}
for (kind, title), (names, counts, mat, order) in panels.items():
    off = mat[~np.eye(len(names), dtype=bool)]
    if kind == "seq":
        print(f"{title} sequence: median {np.median(off):.1f}%, "
              f"range {off.min():.1f}-{off.max():.1f}%, "
              f"pairs >= 95%: {int((off >= 95).sum()) // 2}")
    else:
        print(f"{title} structure: median TM {np.median(off):.2f}, "
              f"range {off.min():.2f}-{off.max():.2f}, "
              f"pairs >= {TM_FOLD_THRESHOLD}: {int((off >= TM_FOLD_THRESHOLD).sum()) // 2}"
              f" of {len(names) * (len(names) - 1) // 2}")
```

## Which complex is which pair

The 18 entries as the grid they actually are, so a cell in any matrix can be
traced back to the complexes it covers.

```{python}
grid = pd.DataFrame({
    "PDB": PDBS,
    "HMA Domain": [short(chain_name(p, 0)) for p in PDBS],
    "Effector": [chain_name(p, 1) for p in PDBS],
    "System": [SYSTEM.get(p, "") for p in PDBS],
}).sort_values(["HMA Domain", "Effector"]).reset_index(drop=True)

n_h, n_e = grid["HMA Domain"].nunique(), grid["Effector"].nunique()
print(f"{n_h} HMA domains x {n_e} effectors = {n_h * n_e} possible pairings, "
      f"{len(grid.drop_duplicates(['HMA Domain', 'Effector']))} solved")
grid
```

## Sequence against structure

The point of doing both. Each dot is one pair of distinct proteins.

```{python}
rows = []
for (col, side, title) in CHAINS:
    names_s, _, ident = grouped_identity(col, side)
    names_t, _, tm, rms = grouped_tm(side)
    pos = {nm: i for i, nm in enumerate(names_t)}
    for a in range(len(names_s)):
        for b in range(a + 1, len(names_s)):
            rows.append({
                "chain": title,
                "pair": f"{short(names_s[a])} / {short(names_s[b])}",
                "identity": ident[a, b],
                "tm": tm[pos[names_s[a]], pos[names_s[b]]],
                "rmsd": rms[pos[names_s[a]], pos[names_s[b]]],
            })
svt = pd.DataFrame(rows)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.6, 6.0))
for title, col in [("HMA Domain", NO_MSA_COLOR), ("Effector", MSA_COLOR)]:
    s = svt[svt["chain"] == title]
    ax.scatter(s["identity"], s["tm"], s=52, color=col, alpha=0.7,
               edgecolor="black", linewidth=0.6, label=title)
ax.axhline(TM_FOLD_THRESHOLD, ls="--", color="grey", lw=1)
ax.text(2, TM_FOLD_THRESHOLD + 0.012, "same fold above this line", va="bottom",
        fontsize=8.5, color="grey")
ax.set_xlabel("Percent sequence identity")
ax.set_ylabel("TM-score")
ax.set_xlim(0, 102)
ax.set_ylim(0, 1.02)
ax.legend(frameon=True, fontsize=9, loc="lower right")
save_fig(fig, "reference_sequence_vs_structure")
plt.show()

low = svt[(svt["identity"] < 30) & (svt["tm"] >= TM_FOLD_THRESHOLD)]
print(f"{len(low)} pairs below 30% identity that still share a fold:")
print(low[["chain", "pair", "identity", "tm", "rmsd"]].round(2)
         .to_string(index=False))
```


- Every pair in the set shares its fold in both chains, including the
  effector pairs that look unrelated by sequence. AVR-Pia against the AVR-Pik
  series sits near 15% identity and still clears 0.5. That is the MAX family
  definition reproduced from the benchmark's own coordinates.
- The sequence effector axis is bimodal, with a gap between 29% and 92%. On
  structure that gap closes to about 0.2 of TM-score.
- The HMA domains behave the same way, only less dramatically, since they were
  never as divergent in sequence to begin with.
- Sequence identity is therefore a poor proxy for how similar two targets look
  to a structure predictor. Two effectors at 15% identity present much the same
  shape.

Caveats. Identity and TM-score are computed on the deposited chains, so a
construct modelled to different boundaries is compared over its resolved
residues only. That is why grouping is by name and every between-group value is
a median. TM-score is a global fold measure, so two chains can score highly
while differing at the binding surface that matters here. A high TM-score is not
a claim that two effectors are interchangeable. UPGMA assumes a roughly constant
rate of change and orders the heatmaps rather than making a phylogenetic
claim.
